details.description: MiniMax-M2.1 is MiniMax's text-only Mixture-of-Experts follow-up to MiniMax-M2, again built with roughly 230 billion total parameters and about 10 billion activated per token. MiniMax describes it as more than a parameter update, aimed at stronger real-world performance on systems, backend, web, mobile, and office-style coding tasks plus multilingual, agent-driven workflows, with faster and more concise responses than M2. It supports function calling and agent scaffolding for tool-using workflows. MiniMax has since released newer text models (M2.5, M2.7, and M3), and M2.1 no longer appears among MiniMax's current models on its site.
advantages: Scores 74.0% on SWE-bench Verified and 72.5% on SWE-bench Multilingual, per MiniMax's model card, up from 69.4% on SWE-bench Verified for the earlier M2.
Scores 47.9% on Terminal-bench 2.0, per MiniMax's model card.
Scores 83.0 on AIME25, 88.0 on MMLU-Pro, and 83.0 on GPQA-Diamond, per MiniMax's model card.
MiniMax reports faster, more concise responses with lower token usage than M2, per Fireworks AI's model listing.
disadvantages: Text-only model that does not accept image or other non-text input, per MiniMax's model card and Fireworks AI's model listing.
MiniMax has since released newer text models (M2.5, M2.7, and M3); M2.1 no longer appears among MiniMax's current models on its site.
use_cases: Backend, web, mobile, and office-style software development tasks
Multilingual, agent-driven coding and tool-use workflows
Long-horizon agentic tool calling requiring concise, efficient responses

sources.title: minimax.io text-model page for the m21 slug (now shows MiniMax M2.5)

notes: Release date still not pinned to a single confirmed day: the HF page's visible 'Jan 5' timestamp resolves in its own markup to 2026-01-05, but the repo itself was created around 2025-12-20 and Fireworks lists it as added 2025-12-23, so the exact public-launch date is somewhere in that Dec 2025-Jan 2026 window; it clearly follows M2 (October 2025) and precedes M2.5, M2.7 and M3, which are now MiniMax's featured text models. Catalog's 204,800-token max input/output roughly matches Fireworks' stated ~196K-token context, so no exact context figure is restated in the description.
